title: Island of Mozambique
summary: The Island of Mozambique is a coral island off northern Mozambique with a stone-and-lime town in the north and a macuti (palm-leaf roof) town in the south. UNESCO says it played a role in Indian Ocean trade from the 10th century and was the first seat of Portuguese colonial government, from 1507 to 1898. Its oldest extant fortress, St. Sebastian, dates to 1558-1620.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO: first seat of the Portuguese colonial government from 1507 to 1898. World History Encyclopedia lists a Portuguese fortress at Mozambique Island in 1507. UNESCO also notes trading links from the 10th century.

as_recorded.value: the first seat of the Portuguese colonial government that lasted from 1507 to 1898
Fortresses were built along the coast of East Africa, notably at Sofala in 1505, Mozambique Island in 1507

where.historical_name: Ilha de Moçambique, Portuguese trading post and colonial capital

importance.justification: UNESCO says it bears witness to the Portuguese maritime routes between Western Europe and the Indian subcontinent.
